text: For the choir director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.
God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem, his dwelling place in Zion.
There he shattered the flashing arrows, the shield and the sword and the weapons of war. Selah
You are radiant with light, more majestic than mountains rich with prey.
The stouthearted lie plundered, sunk in their final sleep; not one of the warriors could lift a hand.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay stunned.

versions.text: At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both horse and rider lay stunned.
versions.explanation: רֶכֶב means "chariot," not "rider." The Hebrew pairs chariot and horse (the war machinery), and the translation should preserve that imagery rather than substituting "rider," which imports language from a different passage.

text: You alone are to be feared. Who can stand before you when your anger flares?
From heaven you pronounced judgment, and the earth was afraid and fell silent,

versions.text: From heaven you pronounced judgment, and the earth was afraid and fell silent
versions.explanation: The line lacks any closing punctuation. Since the sentence carries over into the next verse, a comma at the end signals the continuation and helps an oral reader pace the phrase correctly.

text: when God rose up to judge, to save all the afflicted of the earth. Selah
Even human wrath brings you praise; with the remnant of their rage you gird yourself.

versions.text: Even human wrath brings you praise; the survivors of your fury you gird about yourself.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew שְׁאֵרִית חֵמֹת is "the remnant/residue of wrath(s)" — the same human wrath spoken of in the first line — not "the survivors of your fury." The current wording both adds "your" (absent in Hebrew) and shifts the sense from leftover rage to surviving people, which obscures the parallelism.

text: Make your vows to the LORD your God and keep them; let all the neighboring nations bring gifts to the one who is to be feared.
He breaks the spirit of rulers; he is feared by the kings of the earth.
